[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes Mercury Accuracy is based on version 094 of the bsnes emulator with some accuracy improvements backported from later versions. It is built from the 'performance' profile, which includes bsnes' fastest (but least-accurate) PPU. The biggest problem with the 'performance' profile is that it does not support the CX4 add-on chip used by Capcom's Mega Man X2 and X3 games, but most other games should run fine. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Nuance is a NUON (VM Labs) emulator. NUON was a media-processing architecture embedded in a handful of DVD players (Samsung DVD-N501/N2000, Toshiba SD-2300, RCA DRC-480N) and used to ship a small number of games (Ballistic, Tempest 3000, Merlin Racing, Iron Soldier 3, Freefall 3050 A.D., Space Invaders XL, etc.) on standard DVD discs. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A significantly modified fork of Mednafen's Playstation emulator, this core differs from the -HW version by focusing on software rendering (i.e., instead of hardware-accelerated rendering). The software renderer is more accurate than the OpenGL and Vulkan renderers used in the -HW core, but it lacks some of the cosmetic options and performs any internal resolution increases on the CPU instead of the GPU, which is very demanding (devices with fast CPUs may reach 2x scale but nothing can maintain full speed at 4x at the time of this writing). Both varieties of Beetle-PSX are more accurate than PCSX-ReARMed but also significantly slower, so they are generally a better choice for higher-specced devices that can benefit from the additional features and accuracy while maintaining full speed. extension.summary: Buildbot - Nintendo - Game Boy / Color (TGB Dual)
extension.description: [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the TGB Dual Game Boy emulator to libretro. While this core is a decent, usable emulator, it is most notable for being able to emulate to Game Boys connected via Link Cable, which is useful for things like trading Pokemon, etc. This functionality can be utilized by a second player either locally or via netplay (if supported by the libretro frontend). [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of x16emu, the official emulator of the Commander X16, The 8-Bit Guy's 8-bit computer. Emulates the 65C02 (or 65C816) CPU, the VERA video chip with its PSG and PCM audio, the YM2151 FM synthesizer, the SD card, the real-time clock and up to four SNES controllers, keyboard and mouse. Runs SD card images, PRG programs and BASIC listings.[CR]System: Commander X16[CR]System Manufacturer: The 8-Bit Guy[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Michael Steil|Frank van den Hoef|X16 Community[CR]Supported Files: img|prg|bas|crt[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: x16/rom.bin (Commander X16 KERNAL ROM), Path: x16/rom.bin, Optional: false[CR]Notes: (!) x16/rom.bin: the KERNAL ROM from an x16emu release (github.com/X16Community/x16-emulator/releases), in the system directory.|(!) .img: SD card image; the KERNAL runs AUTOBOOT.X16 from it.|(!) .prg / .bas: loaded and run at start and after every reset. Files next to the content are reachable as device 8.|(!) The RTC NVRAM (KERNAL settings) is kept as the save RAM (.srm).|(!) Use Game Focus (Scroll Lock) to type on the X16 keyboard.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Kronos Saturn emulator, which is itself a port of the Yabause emulator, to libretro. This core supports many modern, fancy features, such as internal resolution increases, though these features come with relatively steep GPU requirements, making this core incompatible with very old, weak or mobile hardware. While not as accurate as Beetle-Saturn, this core's relative speed and eye-candy features make it a good first choice for many users, while those interested in accuracy first-and-foremost should stick with Beetle-Saturn and those on mobile devices should try Yaba Sanshiro (another Yabause fork focused on mobile) instead.[CR]System: Saturn[CR]System Manufacturer: Sega[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Guillaume Duhammel|Theo Berkau|Anders Montonen|devmiyax|FCare|barbudreadmon[CR]Supported Files: ccd|chd|cue|iso|mds|zip|m3u[CR][CR]Firmware Files (4 Total):[CR] File: kronos/saturn_bios.bin (Saturn BIOS), Path: kronos/saturn_bios.bin, Optional: false[CR] File: kronos/stvbios.zip (ST-V BIOS from MAME), Path: kronos/stvbios.zip, Optional: false[CR] File: mpr-18811-mx.ic1 (The King of Fighters '95 ROM Cartridge), Path: mpr-18811-mx.ic1, Optional: true[CR] File: mpr-19367-mx.ic1 (Ultraman: Hikari no Kyojin Densetsu ROM Cartridge), Path: mpr-19367-mx.ic1, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) saturn_bios.bin (md5): af5828fdff51384f99b3c4926be27762|(!) stvbios.zip|(!) mpr-18811-mx.ic1 (md5): 255113ba943c92a54facd25a10fd780c|(!) mpr-19367-mx.ic1 (md5): 1cd19988d1d72a3e7caa0b73234c96b4[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2003 (v0.78), 'MAME 2003-Plus' is compatible with MAME 2003-Plus latest ROM sets. Contributors have backported support for an additional 350 games that are not included in the standard v0.078 ROM set, as well as other functionality not originally present in the underlying codebase. MAME 2003/-Plus cores have tighter integration with libretro features than the more modern snapshots and are significantly faster, though this comes at a substantial reduction in both accuracy and compatibility. These cores are ideal for very weak hardware, such as Raspberry Pi and other Single-Board Computers and consoles, where even FBNeo may be too demanding. If you do not need the additional libretro features and your device can run any newer snapshot core or FBNeo, those are probably better choices for most users.[CR]System: Arcade (various)[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: MAMEdev, MAME 2003-Plus Team, et al (see license and changelog)[CR]Supported Files: zip[CR]Notes: (!) [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of Stella, the multi-platform Atari 2600 VCS emulator, to libretro. This core was forked off from the main Stella codebase circa 2014 and, as such, is a snapshot of the features, compatibility and performance from that time. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the excellent and advanced Playstation Portable (PSP) emulator PPSSPP to libretro. This core runs very fast and is usable on every very modest hardware, while still supporting many advanced features and APIs to provide increased resolution, texture filtering, etc. Aside from the normal libretro frontend features, this core also supports its own native cheats and high-res texture packs by placing them in the core's directory structure that gets created in the frontend's 'saves' directory.[CR]System: PSP[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Henrik Hrydgard[CR]Supported Files: elf|iso|cso|prx|pbp|chd[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: ppge_atlas.zim (PPSSPP Data ROM), Path: PPSSPP/ppge_atlas.zim, Optional: false[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A simulator of various Game and Watch-style handheld electronic games, ported to libretro. Unlike MAME's emulation of these games, which is based on actual emulation, these simulations were created by observing the behavior of the games and then creating new logic that acts similarly. This core is much easier to get up and running than via MAME, so it's a good first choice for playing those games.[CR]System: Handheld Electronic[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Andre Leiradella[CR]Supported Files: mgw[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Cannonball enhanced OutRun engine to libretro. This core includes support for increased framerate (true 60 fps, some 120 fps content), true widescreen, new game modes and many more enhancements. To run the core/game, you will need to extract the contents of an OutRun Revision B ROM archive alongside a dummy file that ends in the *.game file extension (the frontend will load this 'game' file).[CR]System: Outrun Game Engine[CR]System Manufacturer: Sega[CR]System Categories: Game engine[CR]Authors: Chris White[CR]Supported Files: game|88[CR]Notes: (!) You need to have a dummy file with the extension .game inside your MAME rom outrun folder.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the a5200 Atari 5200 emulator to libretro. Based on Atari800 2.0.2 and originally developed for the GCW Zero, this core runs fast on low-powered hardware. With a design focussed on ease of use and good libretro integration, the core is intended as a simple 'plug and play' solution for Atari 5200 content.[CR]System: Atari 5200[CR]System Manufacturer: Atari[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Petr Stehlik|zx81|Alekmaul|wavemotion-dave[CR]Supported Files: a52|bin[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: 5200.rom (5200 BIOS), Path: 5200.rom, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) 5200.rom (md5): 281f20ea4320404ec820fb7ec0693b38[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2016, 'MAME 2016' is compatible with MAME 0.174 ROM sets. MAME is the most compatible emulator in the world, and it can run almost any game from any platform (though running console games through this core requires additional steps). If your device can run the up-to-date MAME - Current core at full speed, most users will have a better experience with that core, while FBNeo is typically a better choice for speed vs accuracy, as long as it supports the game(s) in question. Otherwise, this core is notable as the most recent snapshot core with an unchanging ROM set.[CR]System: Arcade (various)[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: MAMEdev[CR]Supported Files: cmd|zip|7z[CR]Notes: [1] MAME 2016 (0.174) supports MAME save states.|[2] MAME 2016 (0.174) supports extracted MAME cheats.|[3] The BIOS files must be inside the ROM directory.|[4] The same directory with CHD files inside must be inside the ROM directory.|[5] If desired, the ARTWORK, CHEATS, and SAMPLES directories can be|[^] inside the 'SYSTEMDIR\mame' directory.|[6] When saving, the following directories will be created in the 'SAVEDIR\mame'|[^] directory: STATES, NVRAM, INPUT, SNAPS, CFG, MEMCARD, and DIFF.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The VICE PET emulator, isolated and ported to libretro. This core emulates the 2001, 3032, 4032, 8032, 8096, 8296 and SuperPET (MicroMainFrame 9000) models, covering the whole series. Both the 40- and 80-column CRTC video chips are emulated (from the 4032 onward), but a few of the features that are not very important for average applications are not implemented yet, such as numbers of rasterlines per char and lines per screen.[CR]System: PET[CR]System Manufacturer: Commodore[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: VICE Team[CR]Supported Files: d64|d71|d80|d81|d82|g64|g41|x64|t64|tap|prg|p00|crt|bin|zip|gz|d6z|d7z|d8z|g6z|g4z|x6z|cmd|m3u|vfl|vsf|nib|nbz|d2m|d4m|/[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Streams internet radio stations over the network, and plays local MP3 and WAV files. Stations are read from an .m3u or .txt playlist, with up to 100 presets selectable from the core options; the core also starts with no content at all. Draws a spectrum analyser, oscilloscope, VU meters and other visualisers while it plays. Needs a working network connection for streaming.[CR]System: Internet Radio Player[CR]System Categories: Utility[CR]Authors: fpscan|gadsby[CR]Supported Files: m3u|txt|mp3|wav[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A libretro port of current upstream PCSX2, the mature and highly-compatible PlayStation 2 emulator. Unlike the LRPS2 core, which is a hard fork of an older PCSX2, PCEE2 tracks the modern PCSX2 codebase. With the default Vulkan renderer the core renders into a hardware context it negotiates with the frontend; the OpenGL and software renderers hand finished frames over instead. Place a PS2 BIOS dump in 'system/pcsx2/bios' and a copy of the PCSX2 'resources' directory in 'system/pcsx2/resources'. This core is experimental.[CR]System: Sony PlayStation 2[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: PCSX2 Team|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: iso|chd|cso|zso|gz|bin|mdf|nrg|elf|irx[CR][CR]Firmware Files (2 Total):[CR] File: 'pcsx2/bios' folder (any valid PS2 BIOS dump, e.g. scph39001.bin), Path: pcsx2/bios, Optional: false[CR] File: 'pcsx2/resources' folder (shaders, GameIndex.yaml, fonts), Path: pcsx2/resources, Optional: false[CR]Notes: [1] This only checks that the folders exist in the correct location.|[2] The core does not require a specific BIOS filename, so this info file|[^] cannot tell you whether the content of your 'bios' folder is correct.|[3] The 'resources' folder must be copied from a PCSX2 installation of the|[^] same version; the core will not boot without it.|[4] A Vulkan-capable GPU is recommended; the other renderers are less tested.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Snes9x 2002 is a fork of the classic and popular SNES emulator Snes9x from circa 2002. This is the fastest of the Snes9x cores, but it also has the lowest accuracy and worst compatibility. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Snes9x 2005 is a fork of the classic and popular SNES emulator Snes9x from circa 2005. This core is significantly faster than the newer cores, but that speed comes at the price of accuracy, and this core has some bugs in mostly obscure games and lower audio quality. This core is ideal for very weak devices, such as New 3DS and single-board computers. Users who cannot maintain full speed with this core--much less any of the newer Snes9x cores--should fall back to Snes9x 2002 as a last resort.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Snes9x Team|dking|BassAceGold|ShadauxCat|Nebuleon[CR]Supported Files: smc|fig|sfc|gd3|gd7|dx2|bsx|swc[CR]

This is the only choice for users wanting to play PC-98 games, as the meowPC98 and non-Kai NPKII cores are no longer in development and have been completely superseded by this core.[CR]System: PC-98[CR]System Manufacturer: NEC[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Neko Project II Team, Tomohiro Yoshidomi[CR]Supported Files: d98|zip|98d|fdi|fdd|2hd|tfd|d88|88d|hdm|xdf|dup|cmd|hdi|thd|nhd|hdd|hdn[CR][CR]Firmware Files (11 Total):[CR] File: np2kai/font.bmp (needed to display text), Path: np2kai/font.bmp, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/FONT.ROM (alt font file), Path: np2kai/FONT.ROM, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/bios.rom, Path: np2kai/bios.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/itf.rom, Path: np2kai/itf.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/sound.rom, Path: np2kai/sound.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_BD.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_BD.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_SD.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_SD.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_TOP.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_TOP.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_HH.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_HH.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_TOM.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_TOM.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_RIM.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_RIM.WAV, Optional: true[CR]Notes: JOY2KEY buttons mapping: A=x B=z X=space Y=lctrl|L=backspace R=rshift SELECT=escape START=return|Keep 'end' key down when booting for machine options.|Many games need GDC set as 2.5Mhz there.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Jump 'n Bump has no plot, other than that it involves up to four rabbits in multiplayer deathmatch: Dott, Jiffy, Fizz, and Mijji, trying to hop onto each other's heads to squish each other and score a point, while sending gibs flying everywhere. The rabbits are controlled by players on the same computer, using the keyboard, mouse, and/or joystick.[CR]System Manufacturer: Brainchild Design[CR]System Categories: Game engine[CR]Authors: Philippe Simons[CR]Supported Files: dat[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The VICE x64 (fast) Commodore 64 emulator, isolated and ported to libretro. This core features a fairly complete emulation of the VIC-II video chip, with all sprites, registers and video modes emulated in a fully cycle-accurate manner. However, the 'x64sc' core's VIC-II emulation is both cycle-based and pixel-accurate, making it a better choice for devices powerful enough to run it. Both cores include options to switch between the original 'fastSID' sound chip emulation and the slower but much more accurate 'reSID' module.[CR]System: C64[CR]System Manufacturer: Commodore[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: VICE Team[CR]Supported Files: d64|d71|d80|d81|d82|g64|g41|x64|t64|tap|prg|p00|crt|bin|zip|gz|d6z|d7z|d8z|g6z|g4z|x6z|cmd|m3u|vfl|vsf|nib|nbz|d2m|d4m|/[CR][CR]Firmware Files (4 Total):[CR] File: vice/JiffyDOS_C64.bin (JiffyDOS C64 Kernal), Path: vice/JiffyDOS_C64.bin, Optional: true[CR] File: vice/JiffyDOS_1541-II.bin (JiffyDOS 1541 drive BIOS), Path: vice/JiffyDOS_1541-II.bin, Optional: true[CR] File: vice/JiffyDOS_1571_repl310654.bin (JiffyDOS 1571 drive BIOS), Path: vice/JiffyDOS_1571_repl310654.bin, Optional: true[CR] File: vice/JiffyDOS_1581.bin (JiffyDOS 1581 drive BIOS), Path: vice/JiffyDOS_1581.bin, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the Final Burn Alpha codebase from circa 2012, 'FB Alpha 2012 CPS-1' is compatible with FB Alpha v0.2.97.28 ROM sets. This core variant is for CPS-1 games only. It exists solely for use with RAM-constrained platforms, such as certain console or embedded platforms, that do not have the capacity to load the full core along with large games. Most users should use up-to-date FBNeo instead.[CR]System: CP System I[CR]System Manufacturer: Capcom[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Team FB Alpha[CR]Supported Files: zip[CR]Notes: (!) The BIOS files must be inside the ROM directory.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes-jg is a fork of bsnes v115, rewritten to use the C++ standard library and focus on preservation through accurate emulation and a robust, standards-compliant codebase. Speed hacks were removed, and support for achievements and libretro's cheat interface were added. Additionally, higher quality audio resampling, as well as full support for Super Game Boy, BS-X Satellaview, Sufami Turbo, and Competition carts has been implemented. This core is slightly faster than the original bsnes, but still has more or less the same system requirements. It is a great option for desktop platforms with relatively fast CPUs, though it will also run at full speed on a number of ARM SBCs.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Near|Rupert Carmichael[CR]Supported Files: smc|sfc|st|gb|gbc|bs[CR][CR]Firmware Files (16 Total):[CR] File: dsp1.data.rom, Path: dsp1.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1.program.rom, Path: dsp1.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.data.rom, Path: dsp1b.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.program.rom, Path: dsp1b.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.data.rom, Path: dsp2.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.program.rom, Path: dsp2.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.data.rom, Path: dsp3.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.program.rom, Path: dsp3.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.data.rom, Path: dsp4.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.program.rom, Path: dsp4.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.data.rom, Path: st010.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.program.rom, Path: st010.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.data.rom, Path: st011.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.program.rom, Path: st011.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.data.rom, Path: st018.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.program.rom, Path: st018.program.rom, Optional: true[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]An emulator for the TI-83 family of graphing calculators. It is a port of the Wabbitemu emulator to libretro. It allows you to play your TI-83 games like never before in fullscreen using a gamepad. You can also control it with a mouse or keyboard, or you can just use the virtual mouse for navigation.[CR]System: TI83[CR]System Manufacturer: Texas Instruments[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Neil Barkhina|Wabbitemu[CR]Supported Files: 8xp|8xk|8xg[CR][CR]Firmware Files (3 Total):[CR] File: ti83se.rom (TI-83 Silver Edition), Path: ti83se.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: ti83plus.rom (TI-83 Plus), Path: ti83plus.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: ti83.rom (TI-83), Path: ti83.rom, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) ti83se.rom (md5): c6ff8204c5c81b7be34614dbbd690c8b|(!) ti83plus.rom (md5): 8011181f810b5ec4e9d6a03f0e14257a|(!) ti83.rom (md5): d4448d09bbfde687c04f9e3310e023ab[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the RPCS3 PlayStation 3 emulator to libretro. It runs the Cell processor with RPCS3's LLVM recompilers and renders with Vulkan, handing each frame to the frontend through memory, or with OpenGL into the frontend's own context. Needs the PS3 system software (PS3UPDAT.PUP) in the system directory. Save states are not supported.[CR]System: PlayStation 3[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: RPCS3 Team|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: bin|self|elf|iso|pkg|sfo|sfb[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: PS3UPDAT.PUP (PS3 system software), Path: PS3UPDAT.PUP, Optional: false[CR]Notes: (!) PS3UPDAT.PUP is installed on the first run; it may also be in system/rpcs3/.|(!) A game that is not an ISO is loaded by its PS3_DISC.SFB (a disc dump folder) or PARAM.SFO (an installed game).|(!) Game data, saves and the installed firmware live in system/rpcs3/ (dev_hdd0, dev_flash).|(!) Encrypted (redump) ISOs need a .dkey or .key file with the same name, next to the image or in system/rpcs3/data/redump/.|(!) Loading a .pkg installs it and boots the installed game.|(!) The Vulkan renderer (default) works with any video driver; the OpenGL renderer needs the glcore driver and OpenGL 4.5.|(!) Save states are not supported.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]rust-dos, an x86 PC emulator with a DOS of its own: 386 to Pentium MMX, CGA to SVGA, the Tseng ET4000 and the S3 Trio64, a 3dfx Voodoo, Sound Blaster, Gravis Ultrasound, AdLib and General MIDI. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Gambatte Game Boy emulator to libretro. One of the very first libretro cores, this core is reasonably accurate (enough to run all but a scant handful of games with no visible bugs) and blisteringly fast. While Gearboy and SameBoy cores have surpassed it in accuracy, Gambatte is still an excellent choice on low-power systems that cannot handle the more-accurate newcomers while maintaining full speed.[CR]System: Game Boy/Game Boy Color[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Sinamas[CR]Supported Files: gb|gbc|dmg[CR][CR]Firmware Files (2 Total):[CR] File: gb_bios.bin (Game Boy BIOS), Path: gb_bios.bin, Optional: true[CR] File: gbc_bios.bin (Game Boy Color BIOS), Path: gbc_bios.bin, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) gb_bios.bin (md5): 32fbbd84168d3482956eb3c5051637f5|(!) gbc_bios.bin (md5): dbfce9db9deaa2567f6a84fde55f9680[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A fast and portable emulator for many Sega game consoles, ported to libretro. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes Mercury Accuracy is based on version 094 of the bsnes emulator with some accuracy improvements backported from later versions. It also has some optimizations that do not reduce accuracy and some core options that can reduce accuracy (such as overclocking and HLE for the add-on chips used in many carts). It is built from the 'accuracy' profile, which includes bsnes' more-demanding dot-based PPU (as opposed to the faster scanline-precision PPU used in the 'balanced' profile), though the only commercial game that requires this level of precision is the notorious Air Strike Patrol (A.S.P.). The up-to-date bsnes core is a better choice for most users who are seeking the highest accuracy, except for those who require access to cheats and retro-achievements, for whom these older forks may be preferable.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Near|Alcaro[CR]Supported Files: sfc|smc|bml|gb|gbc|st|bs[CR][CR]Firmware Files (18 Total):[CR] File: dsp1.data.rom, Path: dsp1.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1.program.rom, Path: dsp1.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.data.rom, Path: dsp1b.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.program.rom, Path: dsp1b.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.data.rom, Path: dsp2.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.program.rom, Path: dsp2.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.data.rom, Path: dsp3.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.program.rom, Path: dsp3.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.data.rom, Path: dsp4.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.program.rom, Path: dsp4.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: cx4.data.rom, Path: cx4.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.data.rom, Path: st010.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.program.rom, Path: st010.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.data.rom, Path: st011.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.program.rom, Path: st011.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.data.rom, Path: st018.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.program.rom, Path: st018.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: sgb.boot.rom (SGB Boot Image), Path: sgb.boot.rom, Optional: true[CR]Notes: [1] bsnes-mercury Accuracy uses split ROMS for special chip games.|[*] Notable DSP1/DSP1B Games: Super Mario Kart, Pilotwings|[*] Notable DSP2 Games: Dungeon Master|[*] Notable DSP3 Games: SD Gundam GX|[*] Notable DSP4 Games: Top Gear 3000|[*] Notable Cx4 Games: Mega Man X2, Mega Man X3|[2] SGB Emulation will only work with command line.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the mature and well-known DOSBox emulator to libretro. This core is kept up-to-date with the latest sources from DOSBox's SVN trunk and provides some improvements over the DOSBox-SVN core, including native MIDI support (as well as Soundfont-based MIDI support via FluidSynth and BASSMIDI), cycle-accurate OPL3 (YMF262) emulation courtesy of Nuked OPL3, MT-32 emulation courtesy of MUNT and experimental 3dfx Voodoo support. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2000, 'MAME 2000' is compatible with the MAME 0.37b5 ROM set, which was used in the popular iMAME4All port. While this port is the fastest of the libretro cores, it also has the worst accuracy and compatibility, so it should only be used when speed is the utmost concern. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes C++98 is based on version 085 of the bsnes emulator, but with the codebase downgraded to be compatible with the older C++98 standard. It is built from the 'performance' profile, which includes bsnes' fastest (but least-accurate) PPU. This core is really only useful for platforms that are stuck on old compilers (such as certain consoles) that are also powerful enough for bsnes. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The actively maintained Atari Jaguar and Jaguar CD emulator for libretro, continuing the Virtual Jaguar project (originally by David Raingeard of Potato Emulation). No BIOS files are required: the Jaguar boot ROM and CD BIOS images are embedded in the core. Supports Jaguar CD (CUE/BIN, CDI, CHD) with Memory Track saves, JagLink/CatBox network play over TCP or RetroArch netplay, a high-level BIOS that lets most commercial titles boot without a real BIOS image, save states, SRAM, cheat codes, RetroAchievements, and M68K/RISC clock-scale (overclock) core options for framerate-limited games. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Nuance is a NUON (VM Labs) emulator. NUON was a media-processing architecture embedded in a handful of DVD players (Samsung DVD-N501/N2000, Toshiba SD-2300, RCA DRC-480N) and used to ship a small number of games (Ballistic, Tempest 3000, Merlin Racing, Iron Soldier 3, Freefall 3050 A.D., Space Invaders XL, etc.) on standard DVD discs. MAME 2003/-Plus cores have tighter integration with libretro features than the more modern snapshots and are significantly faster, though this comes at a substantial reduction in both accuracy and compatibility. The core renders through a hardware context it shares with the frontend: Vulkan by default, taking the VkInstance and VkPhysicalDevice from the context-negotiation interface and handing finished frames back through set_image, or an OpenGL core 3.3 context (OpenGL ES 3.2 on Android) when the renderer core option asks for it. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A significantly modified fork of Mednafen's Playstation emulator, this core differs from the -HW version by focusing on software rendering (i.e., instead of hardware-accelerated rendering). The software renderer is more accurate than the OpenGL and Vulkan renderers used in the -HW core, but it lacks some of the cosmetic options and performs any internal resolution increases on the CPU instead of the GPU, which is very demanding (devices with fast CPUs may reach 2x scale but nothing can maintain full speed at 4x at the time of this writing). Both varieties of Beetle-PSX are more accurate than PCSX-ReARMed but also significantly slower, so they are generally a better choice for higher-specced devices that can benefit from the additional features and accuracy while maintaining full speed. extension.description: [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the TGB Dual Game Boy emulator to libretro. While this core is a decent, usable emulator, it is most notable for being able to emulate to Game Boys connected via Link Cable, which is useful for things like trading Pokemon, etc. This functionality can be utilized by a second player either locally or via netplay (if supported by the libretro frontend). Emulates the 65C02 (or 65C816) CPU, the VERA video chip with its PSG and PCM audio, the YM2151 FM synthesizer, the SD card, the real-time clock and up to four SNES controllers, keyboard and mouse. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2003 (v0.78), 'MAME 2003-Plus' is compatible with MAME 2003-Plus latest ROM sets. Contributors have backported support for an additional 350 games that are not included in the standard v0.078 ROM set, as well as other functionality not originally present in the underlying codebase. MAME 2003/-Plus cores have tighter integration with libretro features than the more modern snapshots and are significantly faster, though this comes at a substantial reduction in both accuracy and compatibility. These cores are ideal for very weak hardware, such as Raspberry Pi and other Single-Board Computers and consoles, where even FBNeo may be too demanding. If you do not need the additional libretro features and your device can run any newer snapshot core or FBNeo, those are probably better choices for most users.[CR]System: Arcade (various)[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: MAMEdev, MAME 2003-Plus Team, et al (see license and changelog)[CR]Supported Files: zip[CR]Notes: (!) [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A libretro port of current upstream PCSX2, the mature and highly-compatible PlayStation 2 emulator. Unlike the LRPS2 core, which is a hard fork of an older PCSX2, PCEE2 tracks the modern PCSX2 codebase. With the default Vulkan renderer the core renders into a hardware context it negotiates with the frontend; the OpenGL and software renderers hand finished frames over instead. Place a PS2 BIOS dump in 'system/pcsx2/bios' and a copy of the PCSX2 'resources' directory in 'system/pcsx2/resources'. This core is experimental.[CR]System: Sony PlayStation 2[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: PCSX2 Team|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: iso|chd|cso|zso|gz|bin|mdf|nrg|elf|irx[CR][CR]Firmware Files (2 Total):[CR] File: 'pcsx2/bios' folder (any valid PS2 BIOS dump, e.g. scph39001.bin), Path: pcsx2/bios, Optional: false[CR] File: 'pcsx2/resources' folder (shaders, GameIndex.yaml, fonts), Path: pcsx2/resources, Optional: false[CR]Notes: [1] This only checks that the folders exist in the correct location.|[2] The core does not require a specific BIOS filename, so this info file|[^] cannot tell you whether the content of your 'bios' folder is correct.|[3] The 'resources' folder must be copied from a PCSX2 installation of the|[^] same version; the core will not boot without it.|[4] A Vulkan-capable GPU is recommended; the other renderers are less tested.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Snes9x 2005 is a fork of the classic and popular SNES emulator Snes9x from circa 2005. This core is significantly faster than the newer cores, but that speed comes at the price of accuracy, and this core has some bugs in mostly obscure games and lower audio quality. This core is ideal for very weak devices, such as New 3DS and single-board computers. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes-jg is a fork of bsnes v115, rewritten to use the C++ standard library and focus on preservation through accurate emulation and a robust, standards-compliant codebase. Speed hacks were removed, and support for achievements and libretro's cheat interface were added. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The actively maintained Atari Jaguar and Jaguar CD emulator for libretro, continuing the Virtual Jaguar project (originally by David Raingeard of Potato Emulation). No BIOS files are required: the Jaguar boot ROM and CD BIOS images are embedded in the core. Supports Jaguar CD (CUE/BIN, CDI, CHD) with Memory Track saves, JagLink/CatBox network play over TCP or RetroArch netplay, a high-level BIOS that lets most commercial titles boot without a real BIOS image, save states, SRAM, cheat codes, RetroAchievements, and M68K/RISC clock-scale (overclock) core options for framerate-limited games. CHD images must be created with a chdman that writes CHSE session metadata (MAME 2026-08-15 / PR 15886 or later); see the core's jagcd tools. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the PDP11 emulator to libretro. This core emulates the Soviet Electronica BK computers series, including the BK-0010, BK-0010.01 and BK-0011(M), as well as the Terak 8510/a, which is a 1976 American PDP-11/03 platform that the Electronica BK series were designed after. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A libretro port of ARMSX2, a PlayStation 2 emulator forked from PCSX2 and aimed at ARM64 platforms. The core renders through a hardware context it shares with the frontend: Vulkan by default, taking the VkInstance and VkPhysicalDevice from the context-negotiation interface and handing finished frames back through set_image, or an OpenGL core 3.3 context (OpenGL ES 3.2 on Android) when the renderer core option asks for it. A software GS renderer is selectable as well, and presents through that same context. Place a PS2 BIOS dump in 'system/pcsx2/bios' and a copy of the emulator's 'resources' directory in 'system/pcsx2/resources'. Save states, .m3u disc swapping and the usual renderer, upscale and speedhack core options are implemented.[CR]System: Sony PlayStation 2[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: PCSX2 Team|ARMSX2 Team|bmdhacks|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: elf|iso|ciso|chd|cso|zso|bin|mdf|nrg|dump|gz|img|irx|m3u[CR][CR]Firmware Files (2 Total):[CR] File: 'pcsx2/bios' folder (any valid PS2 BIOS dump, e.g. scph39001.bin), Path: pcsx2/bios, Optional: false[CR] File: 'pcsx2/resources' folder (shaders, GameIndex.yaml, fonts), Path: pcsx2/resources, Optional: false[CR]Notes: [1] This only checks that the folders exist in the correct location.|[2] The core does not require a specific BIOS filename, so this info file|[^] cannot tell you whether the content of your 'bios' folder is correct.|[3] The 'resources' folder must be copied from a matching ARMSX2/PCSX2 build;|[^] the core will not boot without it.|[4] The frontend's video driver must be Vulkan or OpenGL, whichever the|[^] renderer core option asks for; the emulator shares that context.|[5] ARM64 only: the buildbot builds Linux aarch64, macOS arm64 and Android|[^] arm64-v8a. On x86-64 use the PCEE2 or LRPS2 core instead.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A significantly modified fork of Mednafen's Playstation emulator, this core differs from the -HW version by focusing on software rendering (i.e., instead of hardware-accelerated rendering). The software renderer is more accurate than the OpenGL and Vulkan renderers used in the -HW core, but it lacks some of the cosmetic options and performs any internal resolution increases on the CPU instead of the GPU, which is very demanding (devices with fast CPUs may reach 2x scale but nothing can maintain full speed at 4x at the time of this writing). Both varieties of Beetle-PSX are more accurate than PCSX-ReARMed but also significantly slower, so they are generally a better choice for higher-specced devices that can benefit from the additional features and accuracy while maintaining full speed. addon.name: Buildbot - Nintendo - Game Boy / Color (TGB Dual)

extension.summary: Buildbot - Nintendo - Game Boy / Color (TGB Dual)
extension.description: [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the TGB Dual Game Boy emulator to libretro. While this core is a decent, usable emulator, it is most notable for being able to emulate to Game Boys connected via Link Cable, which is useful for things like trading Pokemon, etc. This functionality can be utilized by a second player either locally or via netplay (if supported by the libretro frontend). Thanks to the core's modest hardware requirements, it should run well even on low-powered hardware, though users with more powerful hardware may be better served by the SameBoy core, which can also do the same Link Cable functionality but with improved accuracy and compatibility.[CR]System: Game Boy/Game Boy Color[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: GIGO|Hii[CR]Supported Files: cgb|dmg|gb|gbc|sgb[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of x16emu, the official emulator of the Commander X16, The 8-Bit Guy's 8-bit computer. Emulates the 65C02 (or 65C816) CPU, the VERA video chip with its PSG and PCM audio, the YM2151 FM synthesizer, the SD card, the real-time clock and up to four SNES controllers, keyboard and mouse. Runs SD card images, PRG programs and BASIC listings.[CR]System: Commander X16[CR]System Manufacturer: The 8-Bit Guy[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Michael Steil|Frank van den Hoef|X16 Community[CR]Supported Files: img|prg|bas|crt[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: x16/rom.bin (Commander X16 KERNAL ROM), Path: x16/rom.bin, Optional: false[CR]Notes: (!) x16/rom.bin: the KERNAL ROM from an x16emu release (github.com/X16Community/x16-emulator/releases), in the system directory.|(!) .img: SD card image; the KERNAL runs AUTOBOOT.X16 from it.|(!) .prg / .bas: loaded and run at start and after every reset. Files next to the content are reachable as device 8.|(!) The RTC NVRAM (KERNAL settings) is kept as the save RAM (.srm).|(!) Use Game Focus (Scroll Lock) to type on the X16 keyboard.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2003 (v0.78), 'MAME 2003-Plus' is compatible with MAME 2003-Plus latest ROM sets. Contributors have backported support for an additional 350 games that are not included in the standard v0.078 ROM set, as well as other functionality not originally present in the underlying codebase. MAME 2003/-Plus cores have tighter integration with libretro features than the more modern snapshots and are significantly faster, though this comes at a substantial reduction in both accuracy and compatibility. These cores are ideal for very weak hardware, such as Raspberry Pi and other Single-Board Computers and consoles, where even FBNeo may be too demanding. If you do not need the additional libretro features and your device can run any newer snapshot core or FBNeo, those are probably better choices for most users.[CR]System: Arcade (various)[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: MAMEdev, MAME 2003-Plus Team, et al (see license and changelog)[CR]Supported Files: zip[CR]Notes: (!) [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of Stella, the multi-platform Atari 2600 VCS emulator, to libretro. This core was forked off from the main Stella codebase circa 2014 and, as such, is a snapshot of the features, compatibility and performance from that time. Unlike MAME's emulation of these games, which is based on actual emulation, these simulations were created by observing the behavior of the games and then creating new logic that acts similarly. Based on Atari800 2.0.2 and originally developed for the GCW Zero, this core runs fast on low-powered hardware. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2016, 'MAME 2016' is compatible with MAME 0.174 ROM sets. MAME is the most compatible emulator in the world, and it can run almost any game from any platform (though running console games through this core requires additional steps). If your device can run the up-to-date MAME - Current core at full speed, most users will have a better experience with that core, while FBNeo is typically a better choice for speed vs accuracy, as long as it supports the game(s) in question. Otherwise, this core is notable as the most recent snapshot core with an unchanging ROM set.[CR]System: Arcade (various)[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: MAMEdev[CR]Supported Files: cmd|zip|7z[CR]Notes: [1] MAME 2016 (0.174) supports MAME save states.|[2] MAME 2016 (0.174) supports extracted MAME cheats.|[3] The BIOS files must be inside the ROM directory.|[4] The same directory with CHD files inside must be inside the ROM directory.|[5] If desired, the ARTWORK, CHEATS, and SAMPLES directories can be|[^] inside the 'SYSTEMDIR\mame' directory.|[6] When saving, the following directories will be created in the 'SAVEDIR\mame'|[^] directory: STATES, NVRAM, INPUT, SNAPS, CFG, MEMCARD, and DIFF.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The VICE PET emulator, isolated and ported to libretro. This core emulates the 2001, 3032, 4032, 8032, 8096, 8296 and SuperPET (MicroMainFrame 9000) models, covering the whole series. Both the 40- and 80-column CRTC video chips are emulated (from the 4032 onward), but a few of the features that are not very important for average applications are not implemented yet, such as numbers of rasterlines per char and lines per screen.[CR]System: PET[CR]System Manufacturer: Commodore[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: VICE Team[CR]Supported Files: d64|d71|d80|d81|d82|g64|g41|x64|t64|tap|prg|p00|crt|bin|zip|gz|d6z|d7z|d8z|g6z|g4z|x6z|cmd|m3u|vfl|vsf|nib|nbz|d2m|d4m|/[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Streams internet radio stations over the network, and plays local MP3 and WAV files. Stations are read from an .m3u or .txt playlist, with up to 100 presets selectable from the core options; the core also starts with no content at all. Draws a spectrum analyser, oscilloscope, VU meters and other visualisers while it plays. Needs a working network connection for streaming.[CR]System: Internet Radio Player[CR]System Categories: Utility[CR]Authors: fpscan|gadsby[CR]Supported Files: m3u|txt|mp3|wav[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A libretro port of current upstream PCSX2, the mature and highly-compatible PlayStation 2 emulator. Unlike the LRPS2 core, which is a hard fork of an older PCSX2, PCEE2 tracks the modern PCSX2 codebase. With the default Vulkan renderer the core renders into a hardware context it negotiates with the frontend; the OpenGL and software renderers hand finished frames over instead. Place a PS2 BIOS dump in 'system/pcsx2/bios' and a copy of the PCSX2 'resources' directory in 'system/pcsx2/resources'. This core is experimental.[CR]System: Sony PlayStation 2[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: PCSX2 Team|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: iso|chd|cso|zso|gz|bin|mdf|nrg|elf|irx[CR][CR]Firmware Files (2 Total):[CR] File: 'pcsx2/bios' folder (any valid PS2 BIOS dump, e.g. scph39001.bin), Path: pcsx2/bios, Optional: false[CR] File: 'pcsx2/resources' folder (shaders, GameIndex.yaml, fonts), Path: pcsx2/resources, Optional: false[CR]Notes: [1] This only checks that the folders exist in the correct location.|[2] The core does not require a specific BIOS filename, so this info file|[^] cannot tell you whether the content of your 'bios' folder is correct.|[3] The 'resources' folder must be copied from a PCSX2 installation of the|[^] same version; the core will not boot without it.|[4] A Vulkan-capable GPU is recommended; the other renderers are less tested.[CR]

This is the fastest of the Snes9x cores, but it also has the lowest accuracy and worst compatibility. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Snes9x 2005 is a fork of the classic and popular SNES emulator Snes9x from circa 2005. This core is significantly faster than the newer cores, but that speed comes at the price of accuracy, and this core has some bugs in mostly obscure games and lower audio quality. This core is ideal for very weak devices, such as New 3DS and single-board computers. Users who cannot maintain full speed with this core--much less any of the newer Snes9x cores--should fall back to Snes9x 2002 as a last resort.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Snes9x Team|dking|BassAceGold|ShadauxCat|Nebuleon[CR]Supported Files: smc|fig|sfc|gd3|gd7|dx2|bsx|swc[CR]

This is the only choice for users wanting to play PC-98 games, as the meowPC98 and non-Kai NPKII cores are no longer in development and have been completely superseded by this core.[CR]System: PC-98[CR]System Manufacturer: NEC[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Neko Project II Team, Tomohiro Yoshidomi[CR]Supported Files: d98|zip|98d|fdi|fdd|2hd|tfd|d88|88d|hdm|xdf|dup|cmd|hdi|thd|nhd|hdd|hdn[CR][CR]Firmware Files (11 Total):[CR] File: np2kai/font.bmp (needed to display text), Path: np2kai/font.bmp, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/FONT.ROM (alt font file), Path: np2kai/FONT.ROM, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/bios.rom, Path: np2kai/bios.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/itf.rom, Path: np2kai/itf.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/sound.rom, Path: np2kai/sound.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_BD.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_BD.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_SD.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_SD.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_TOP.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_TOP.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_HH.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_HH.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_TOM.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_TOM.WAV, Optional: true[CR] File: np2kai/2608_RIM.WAV (YM2608 rhythm sample), Path: np2kai/2608_RIM.WAV, Optional: true[CR]Notes: JOY2KEY buttons mapping: A=x B=z X=space Y=lctrl|L=backspace R=rshift SELECT=escape START=return|Keep 'end' key down when booting for machine options.|Many games need GDC set as 2.5Mhz there.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Jump 'n Bump has no plot, other than that it involves up to four rabbits in multiplayer deathmatch: Dott, Jiffy, Fizz, and Mijji, trying to hop onto each other's heads to squish each other and score a point, while sending gibs flying everywhere. The rabbits are controlled by players on the same computer, using the keyboard, mouse, and/or joystick.[CR]System Manufacturer: Brainchild Design[CR]System Categories: Game engine[CR]Authors: Philippe Simons[CR]Supported Files: dat[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The VICE x64 (fast) Commodore 64 emulator, isolated and ported to libretro. This core features a fairly complete emulation of the VIC-II video chip, with all sprites, registers and video modes emulated in a fully cycle-accurate manner. However, the 'x64sc' core's VIC-II emulation is both cycle-based and pixel-accurate, making it a better choice for devices powerful enough to run it. Both cores include options to switch between the original 'fastSID' sound chip emulation and the slower but much more accurate 'reSID' module.[CR]System: C64[CR]System Manufacturer: Commodore[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: VICE Team[CR]Supported Files: d64|d71|d80|d81|d82|g64|g41|x64|t64|tap|prg|p00|crt|bin|zip|gz|d6z|d7z|d8z|g6z|g4z|x6z|cmd|m3u|vfl|vsf|nib|nbz|d2m|d4m|/[CR][CR]Firmware Files (4 Total):[CR] File: vice/JiffyDOS_C64.bin (JiffyDOS C64 Kernal), Path: vice/JiffyDOS_C64.bin, Optional: true[CR] File: vice/JiffyDOS_1541-II.bin (JiffyDOS 1541 drive BIOS), Path: vice/JiffyDOS_1541-II.bin, Optional: true[CR] File: vice/JiffyDOS_1571_repl310654.bin (JiffyDOS 1571 drive BIOS), Path: vice/JiffyDOS_1571_repl310654.bin, Optional: true[CR] File: vice/JiffyDOS_1581.bin (JiffyDOS 1581 drive BIOS), Path: vice/JiffyDOS_1581.bin, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the Final Burn Alpha codebase from circa 2012, 'FB Alpha 2012 CPS-1' is compatible with FB Alpha v0.2.97.28 ROM sets. This core variant is for CPS-1 games only. It exists solely for use with RAM-constrained platforms, such as certain console or embedded platforms, that do not have the capacity to load the full core along with large games. Most users should use up-to-date FBNeo instead.[CR]System: CP System I[CR]System Manufacturer: Capcom[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Team FB Alpha[CR]Supported Files: zip[CR]Notes: (!) The BIOS files must be inside the ROM directory.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes-jg is a fork of bsnes v115, rewritten to use the C++ standard library and focus on preservation through accurate emulation and a robust, standards-compliant codebase. Speed hacks were removed, and support for achievements and libretro's cheat interface were added. Additionally, higher quality audio resampling, as well as full support for Super Game Boy, BS-X Satellaview, Sufami Turbo, and Competition carts has been implemented. This core is slightly faster than the original bsnes, but still has more or less the same system requirements. It is a great option for desktop platforms with relatively fast CPUs, though it will also run at full speed on a number of ARM SBCs.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Near|Rupert Carmichael[CR]Supported Files: smc|sfc|st|gb|gbc|bs[CR][CR]Firmware Files (16 Total):[CR] File: dsp1.data.rom, Path: dsp1.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1.program.rom, Path: dsp1.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.data.rom, Path: dsp1b.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.program.rom, Path: dsp1b.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.data.rom, Path: dsp2.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.program.rom, Path: dsp2.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.data.rom, Path: dsp3.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.program.rom, Path: dsp3.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.data.rom, Path: dsp4.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.program.rom, Path: dsp4.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.data.rom, Path: st010.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.program.rom, Path: st010.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.data.rom, Path: st011.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.program.rom, Path: st011.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.data.rom, Path: st018.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.program.rom, Path: st018.program.rom, Optional: true[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]An emulator for the TI-83 family of graphing calculators. It is a port of the Wabbitemu emulator to libretro. It allows you to play your TI-83 games like never before in fullscreen using a gamepad. You can also control it with a mouse or keyboard, or you can just use the virtual mouse for navigation.[CR]System: TI83[CR]System Manufacturer: Texas Instruments[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Neil Barkhina|Wabbitemu[CR]Supported Files: 8xp|8xk|8xg[CR][CR]Firmware Files (3 Total):[CR] File: ti83se.rom (TI-83 Silver Edition), Path: ti83se.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: ti83plus.rom (TI-83 Plus), Path: ti83plus.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: ti83.rom (TI-83), Path: ti83.rom, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) ti83se.rom (md5): c6ff8204c5c81b7be34614dbbd690c8b|(!) ti83plus.rom (md5): 8011181f810b5ec4e9d6a03f0e14257a|(!) ti83.rom (md5): d4448d09bbfde687c04f9e3310e023ab[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the RPCS3 PlayStation 3 emulator to libretro. It runs the Cell processor with RPCS3's LLVM recompilers and renders with Vulkan, handing each frame to the frontend through memory, or with OpenGL into the frontend's own context. Needs the PS3 system software (PS3UPDAT.PUP) in the system directory. Save states are not supported.[CR]System: PlayStation 3[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: RPCS3 Team|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: bin|self|elf|iso|pkg|sfo|sfb[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: PS3UPDAT.PUP (PS3 system software), Path: PS3UPDAT.PUP, Optional: false[CR]Notes: (!) PS3UPDAT.PUP is installed on the first run; it may also be in system/rpcs3/.|(!) A game that is not an ISO is loaded by its PS3_DISC.SFB (a disc dump folder) or PARAM.SFO (an installed game).|(!) Game data, saves and the installed firmware live in system/rpcs3/ (dev_hdd0, dev_flash).|(!) Encrypted (redump) ISOs need a .dkey or .key file with the same name, next to the image or in system/rpcs3/data/redump/.|(!) Loading a .pkg installs it and boots the installed game.|(!) The Vulkan renderer (default) works with any video driver; the OpenGL renderer needs the glcore driver and OpenGL 4.5.|(!) Save states are not supported.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]rust-dos, an x86 PC emulator with a DOS of its own: 386 to Pentium MMX, CGA to SVGA, the Tseng ET4000 and the S3 Trio64, a 3dfx Voodoo, Sound Blaster, Gravis Ultrasound, AdLib and General MIDI. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Gambatte Game Boy emulator to libretro. One of the very first libretro cores, this core is reasonably accurate (enough to run all but a scant handful of games with no visible bugs) and blisteringly fast. While Gearboy and SameBoy cores have surpassed it in accuracy, Gambatte is still an excellent choice on low-power systems that cannot handle the more-accurate newcomers while maintaining full speed.[CR]System: Game Boy/Game Boy Color[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Sinamas[CR]Supported Files: gb|gbc|dmg[CR][CR]Firmware Files (2 Total):[CR] File: gb_bios.bin (Game Boy BIOS), Path: gb_bios.bin, Optional: true[CR] File: gbc_bios.bin (Game Boy Color BIOS), Path: gbc_bios.bin, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) gb_bios.bin (md5): 32fbbd84168d3482956eb3c5051637f5|(!) gbc_bios.bin (md5): dbfce9db9deaa2567f6a84fde55f9680[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A fast and portable emulator for many Sega game consoles, ported to libretro. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes Mercury Accuracy is based on version 094 of the bsnes emulator with some accuracy improvements backported from later versions. It also has some optimizations that do not reduce accuracy and some core options that can reduce accuracy (such as overclocking and HLE for the add-on chips used in many carts). It is built from the 'accuracy' profile, which includes bsnes' more-demanding dot-based PPU (as opposed to the faster scanline-precision PPU used in the 'balanced' profile), though the only commercial game that requires this level of precision is the notorious Air Strike Patrol (A.S.P.). The up-to-date bsnes core is a better choice for most users who are seeking the highest accuracy, except for those who require access to cheats and retro-achievements, for whom these older forks may be preferable.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Near|Alcaro[CR]Supported Files: sfc|smc|bml|gb|gbc|st|bs[CR][CR]Firmware Files (18 Total):[CR] File: dsp1.data.rom, Path: dsp1.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1.program.rom, Path: dsp1.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.data.rom, Path: dsp1b.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.program.rom, Path: dsp1b.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.data.rom, Path: dsp2.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.program.rom, Path: dsp2.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.data.rom, Path: dsp3.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.program.rom, Path: dsp3.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.data.rom, Path: dsp4.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.program.rom, Path: dsp4.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: cx4.data.rom, Path: cx4.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.data.rom, Path: st010.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.program.rom, Path: st010.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.data.rom, Path: st011.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.program.rom, Path: st011.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.data.rom, Path: st018.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.program.rom, Path: st018.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: sgb.boot.rom (SGB Boot Image), Path: sgb.boot.rom, Optional: true[CR]Notes: [1] bsnes-mercury Accuracy uses split ROMS for special chip games.|[*] Notable DSP1/DSP1B Games: Super Mario Kart, Pilotwings|[*] Notable DSP2 Games: Dungeon Master|[*] Notable DSP3 Games: SD Gundam GX|[*] Notable DSP4 Games: Top Gear 3000|[*] Notable Cx4 Games: Mega Man X2, Mega Man X3|[2] SGB Emulation will only work with command line.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the popular Dolphin Gamecube/Wii emulator to libretro. This core exposes only a subset of the many features included in the standalone Dolphin emulator, but it can provide a simplified and libretro-native experience for playing these games. The core needs the 'Sys' directory copied from the standalone emulator's files into the frontend's system directory, as this is where the emulator looks to apply per-game settings/hacks for better compatibility and performance. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes C++98 is based on version 085 of the bsnes emulator, but with the codebase downgraded to be compatible with the older C++98 standard. It is built from the 'performance' profile, which includes bsnes' fastest (but least-accurate) PPU. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The actively maintained Atari Jaguar and Jaguar CD emulator for libretro, continuing the Virtual Jaguar project (originally by David Raingeard of Potato Emulation). No BIOS files are required: the Jaguar boot ROM and CD BIOS images are embedded in the core. Supports Jaguar CD (CUE/BIN, CDI, CHD) with Memory Track saves, JagLink/CatBox network play over TCP or RetroArch netplay, a high-level BIOS that lets most commercial titles boot without a real BIOS image, save states, SRAM, cheat codes, RetroAchievements, and M68K/RISC clock-scale (overclock) core options for framerate-limited games. CHD images must be created with a chdman that writes CHSE session metadata (MAME 2026-08-15 / PR 15886 or later); see the core's jagcd tools. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the PDP11 emulator to libretro. This core emulates the Soviet Electronica BK computers series, including the BK-0010, BK-0010.01 and BK-0011(M), as well as the Terak 8510/a, which is a 1976 American PDP-11/03 platform that the Electronica BK series were designed after. The BK series computers were the first mass-produced, affordable personal computers in Russia in the 1980s and they had a tremendous effect on the development of the Russian-speaking software community, similar to the C64, ZX Spectrum and Atari 2600 communities elsewhere in the world. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Nuance is a NUON (VM Labs) emulator. NUON was a media-processing architecture embedded in a handful of DVD players (Samsung DVD-N501/N2000, Toshiba SD-2300, RCA DRC-480N) and used to ship a small number of games (Ballistic, Tempest 3000, Merlin Racing, Iron Soldier 3, Freefall 3050 A.D., Space Invaders XL, etc.) on standard DVD discs. The Linux/libretro port adds an OpenGL render path, miniaudio output, FUSE/ISO9660 disc reading, and an asmjit-based 64-bit JIT (x86_64; other architectures run the interpreter) on top of the original Windows codebase. Considered experimental. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes 2014 Balanced is based on version 094 of the bsnes emulator with some accuracy improvements backported from later versions. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A libretro port of ARMSX2, a PlayStation 2 emulator forked from PCSX2 and aimed at ARM64 platforms. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A significantly modified fork of Mednafen's Playstation emulator, this core differs from the non-HW version by providing GPU-accelerated renderers for OpenGL and Vulkan. These renderers provide increased internal resolution for smooth, high-res polygons with minimal performance impact, texture filtering and other cosmetic changes. Both varieties of Beetle-PSX are more accurate than PCSX-ReARMed but also significantly slower, so they are generally a better choice for higher-specced devices that can benefit from the additional features and accuracy while maintaining full speed. This core represents an imaginary handheld game console inspired by real 8- and 16-bit systems that is intended for simple games that can be programmed in second-generation, structured BASIC. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A significantly modified fork of Mednafen's Playstation emulator, this core differs from the -HW version by focusing on software rendering (i.e., instead of hardware-accelerated rendering). The software renderer is more accurate than the OpenGL and Vulkan renderers used in the -HW core, but it lacks some of the cosmetic options and performs any internal resolution increases on the CPU instead of the GPU, which is very demanding (devices with fast CPUs may reach 2x scale but nothing can maintain full speed at 4x at the time of this writing). Both varieties of Beetle-PSX are more accurate than PCSX-ReARMed but also significantly slower, so they are generally a better choice for higher-specced devices that can benefit from the additional features and accuracy while maintaining full speed. extension.summary: Buildbot - Nintendo - Game Boy / Color (TGB Dual)
extension.description: [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the TGB Dual Game Boy emulator to libretro. While this core is a decent, usable emulator, it is most notable for being able to emulate to Game Boys connected via Link Cable, which is useful for things like trading Pokemon, etc. This functionality can be utilized by a second player either locally or via netplay (if supported by the libretro frontend). Thanks to the core's modest hardware requirements, it should run well even on low-powered hardware, though users with more powerful hardware may be better served by the SameBoy core, which can also do the same Link Cable functionality but with improved accuracy and compatibility.[CR]System: Game Boy/Game Boy Color[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: GIGO|Hii[CR]Supported Files: cgb|dmg|gb|gbc|sgb[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of x16emu, the official emulator of the Commander X16, The 8-Bit Guy's 8-bit computer. Emulates the 65C02 (or 65C816) CPU, the VERA video chip with its PSG and PCM audio, the YM2151 FM synthesizer, the SD card, the real-time clock and up to four SNES controllers, keyboard and mouse. Runs SD card images, PRG programs and BASIC listings.[CR]System: Commander X16[CR]System Manufacturer: The 8-Bit Guy[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Michael Steil|Frank van den Hoef|X16 Community[CR]Supported Files: img|prg|bas|crt[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: x16/rom.bin (Commander X16 KERNAL ROM), Path: x16/rom.bin, Optional: false[CR]Notes: (!) x16/rom.bin: the KERNAL ROM from an x16emu release (github.com/X16Community/x16-emulator/releases), in the system directory.|(!) .img: SD card image; the KERNAL runs AUTOBOOT.X16 from it.|(!) .prg / .bas: loaded and run at start and after every reset. Files next to the content are reachable as device 8.|(!) The RTC NVRAM (KERNAL settings) is kept as the save RAM (.srm).|(!) Use Game Focus (Scroll Lock) to type on the X16 keyboard.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2003 (v0.78), 'MAME 2003-Plus' is compatible with MAME 2003-Plus latest ROM sets. Contributors have backported support for an additional 350 games that are not included in the standard v0.078 ROM set, as well as other functionality not originally present in the underlying codebase. MAME 2003/-Plus cores have tighter integration with libretro features than the more modern snapshots and are significantly faster, though this comes at a substantial reduction in both accuracy and compatibility. These cores are ideal for very weak hardware, such as Raspberry Pi and other Single-Board Computers and consoles, where even FBNeo may be too demanding. If you do not need the additional libretro features and your device can run any newer snapshot core or FBNeo, those are probably better choices for most users.[CR]System: Arcade (various)[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: MAMEdev, MAME 2003-Plus Team, et al (see license and changelog)[CR]Supported Files: zip[CR]Notes: (!) [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of Stella, the multi-platform Atari 2600 VCS emulator, to libretro. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Genesis Plus GX emulator to libretro. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2016, 'MAME 2016' is compatible with MAME 0.174 ROM sets. MAME is the most compatible emulator in the world, and it can run almost any game from any platform (though running console games through this core requires additional steps). If your device can run the up-to-date MAME - Current core at full speed, most users will have a better experience with that core, while FBNeo is typically a better choice for speed vs accuracy, as long as it supports the game(s) in question. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The VICE x64 (fast) Commodore 64 emulator, isolated and ported to libretro. This core features a fairly complete emulation of the VIC-II video chip, with all sprites, registers and video modes emulated in a fully cycle-accurate manner. However, the 'x64sc' core's VIC-II emulation is both cycle-based and pixel-accurate, making it a better choice for devices powerful enough to run it. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes-jg is a fork of bsnes v115, rewritten to use the C++ standard library and focus on preservation through accurate emulation and a robust, standards-compliant codebase. Speed hacks were removed, and support for achievements and libretro's cheat interface were added. Additionally, higher quality audio resampling, as well as full support for Super Game Boy, BS-X Satellaview, Sufami Turbo, and Competition carts has been implemented. This core is slightly faster than the original bsnes, but still has more or less the same system requirements. It is a great option for desktop platforms with relatively fast CPUs, though it will also run at full speed on a number of ARM SBCs.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Near|Rupert Carmichael[CR]Supported Files: smc|sfc|st|gb|gbc|bs[CR][CR]Firmware Files (16 Total):[CR] File: dsp1.data.rom, Path: dsp1.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1.program.rom, Path: dsp1.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.data.rom, Path: dsp1b.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp1b.program.rom, Path: dsp1b.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.data.rom, Path: dsp2.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp2.program.rom, Path: dsp2.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.data.rom, Path: dsp3.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp3.program.rom, Path: dsp3.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.data.rom, Path: dsp4.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: dsp4.program.rom, Path: dsp4.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.data.rom, Path: st010.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st010.program.rom, Path: st010.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.data.rom, Path: st011.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st011.program.rom, Path: st011.program.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.data.rom, Path: st018.data.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: st018.program.rom, Path: st018.program.rom, Optional: true[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the RPCS3 PlayStation 3 emulator to libretro. It runs the Cell processor with RPCS3's LLVM recompilers and renders with Vulkan, handing each frame to the frontend through memory, or with OpenGL into the frontend's own context. Needs the PS3 system software (PS3UPDAT.PUP) in the system directory. Save states are not supported.[CR]System: PlayStation 3[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: RPCS3 Team|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: bin|self|elf|iso|pkg|sfo|sfb[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: PS3UPDAT.PUP (PS3 system software), Path: PS3UPDAT.PUP, Optional: false[CR]Notes: (!) PS3UPDAT.PUP is installed on the first run; it may also be in system/rpcs3/.|(!) A game that is not an ISO is loaded by its PS3_DISC.SFB (a disc dump folder) or PARAM.SFO (an installed game).|(!) Game data, saves and the installed firmware live in system/rpcs3/ (dev_hdd0, dev_flash).|(!) Encrypted (redump) ISOs need a .dkey or .key file with the same name, next to the image or in system/rpcs3/data/redump/.|(!) Loading a .pkg installs it and boots the installed game.|(!) The Vulkan renderer (default) works with any video driver; the OpenGL renderer needs the glcore driver and OpenGL 4.5.|(!) Save states are not supported.[CR]

extension.summary: Buildbot - Nintendo - Game Boy Advance (VBA Next)
extension.description: [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A fork of the venerable Game Boy Advance emulator, VisualBoy Advance-Merged, branched off circa 2011, but with some backported patches for improved performance and compatibility. This core runs a bit faster than the up-to-date VBA-M core, but it is based on an older snapshot of the codebase and lacks many years of development and improvements, resulting in compatibility issues with some games (mostly related to a lack of support for the tilt and solar sensors). [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]An N64 emulator based originally on Mupen64Plus, but with extensive changes that have caused the codebases to diverge significantly. This core was the first N64 emulator core available for libretro and has served as an experimental testbed for many features that were later included in the Mupen64plus-Next core, including the advanced Vulkan-based ParaLLEl-RDP and ParaLLEl-RSP plugins (hence the name). [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes C++98 is based on version 085 of the bsnes emulator, but with the codebase downgraded to be compatible with the older C++98 standard. It is built from the 'performance' profile, which includes bsnes' fastest (but least-accurate) PPU. This core is really only useful for platforms that are stuck on old compilers (such as certain consoles) that are also powerful enough for bsnes. This core supports Atari's 16-/32-bit ST/STE/TT/Falcon hardware and, unlike many other ST emulators that just try to give a good environment for running GEM applications, Hatari tries to emulate the hardware as closely as possible, so it can support most of the old Atari games and demos. The core requires a TOS image to function and supports m3u playlists for use with multi-disk games. This core is a good option for most users on a modern device.[CR]System: Atari ST/STE/TT/Falcon[CR]System Manufacturer: Atari[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Nicolas Pomarède[CR]Supported Files: st|msa|zip|stx|dim|ipf|vhd|gem|ide|m3u[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: tos.img (TOS 1.02 US aka Mega TOS), Path: tos.img, Optional: false[CR]Notes: (!) tos.img (md5): c1c57ce48e8ee4135885cee9e63a68a2[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the highly accurate Sega 8-bit console emulator Gearsystem to libretro. This core supports Sega's Mark III, Master System, Game Gear and Game 1000 (SG-1000) consoles, along with the Othello Multivision. It faithfully emulates all of the hardware, including undocumented features of the Z80 CPU. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Cemu Wii U emulator to libretro. Renders through the frontend's hardware context, either Vulkan (sharing RetroArch's instance, device and queue) or OpenGL 4.5 core profile, and can composite the GamePad (DRC) screen next to the TV screen in several layouts. Save states are not supported and never will be, as Cemu has no infrastructure for serializing emulator state.[CR]System: Wii U[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Cemu Project|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: wud|wux|wua|iso|rpx|elf|tmd[CR][CR]Firmware Files (0 Total):[CR][CR]Notes: (!) Save states are not supported - Cemu has no state serialization.|(!) Requires keys.txt in system/Cemu/ to load encrypted titles.|(!) MLC storage is created in saves/Cemu/mlc01/.|(!) Shared fonts go in system/Cemu/resources/sharedFonts/, graphic packs in system/Cemu/graphicPacks/.|(!) Needs a Vulkan or OpenGL 4.5 capable GPU. On Wayland use the Vulkan graphics API core option - the OpenGL path renders black there.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]FCEUmm libretro is based on the FCEUmm (mappers modified) fork of the FCEU emulator. It is very fast and supports many mappers, including those for weird, obscure bootleg carts. It is tightly integrated with libretro features, which makes it a good choice for users seeking advanced frontend functionality, such as runahead and rollback netplay. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A work-in-progress port of EightyOne (a.k.a. THE Sinclair Emulator) to libretro. The core currently only emulates the Sinclair ZX81 with 16Kb RAM and correctly loads and runs many games in the p and tzx formats. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]An up-to-date port of the Mupen64Plus N64 emulator, ported to libretro. It uses up-to-date GLideN64 plugin as its default graphics plug, though the high-accuracy Angrylion and ParaLLEl-RDP plugins are also available. This core is a good first choice for most users and should generally work better than the ParaLLEl-N64 core, which is mainly useful for its support for legacy graphics plugins that can run on older/low-power devices that are too weak for the modern plugins. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The actively maintained Atari Jaguar and Jaguar CD emulator for libretro, continuing the Virtual Jaguar project (originally by David Raingeard of Potato Emulation). No BIOS files are required: the Jaguar boot ROM and CD BIOS images are embedded in the core. Supports Jaguar CD (CUE/BIN, CDI, CHD) with Memory Track saves, JagLink/CatBox network play over TCP or RetroArch netplay, a high-level BIOS that lets most commercial titles boot without a real BIOS image, save states, SRAM, cheat codes, RetroAchievements, and M68K/RISC clock-scale (overclock) core options for framerate-limited games. CHD images must be created with a chdman that writes CHSE session metadata (MAME 2026-08-15 / PR 15886 or later); see the core's jagcd tools. The accurate blitter is SIMD-accelerated (SSE2 on x86, NEON on ARM); the Blitter core option can be set to 'Fast' to trade some accuracy for additional speed on lower-end hardware.[CR]System: Jaguar[CR]System Manufacturer: Atari[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Joseph Mattiello|David Raingeard|Shamus[CR]Supported Files: j64|jag|rom|abs|cof|bin|prg|cue|cdi|chd[CR][CR]Firmware Files (4 Total):[CR] File: [BIOS] Atari Jaguar CD (World).j64 (Jaguar CD BIOS, retail - optional override), Path: [BIOS] Atari Jaguar CD (World).j64, Optional: true[CR] File: [BIOS] Atari Jaguar Developer CD (World).j64 (Jaguar CD BIOS, developer - optional override), Path: [BIOS] Atari Jaguar Developer CD (World).j64, Optional: true[CR] File: jagboot_m.rom (Jaguar cart boot ROM, Model M - optional override), Path: jagboot_m.rom, Optional: true[CR] File: jagboot.rom (Jaguar cart boot ROM, any revision - optional, used when Cart BIOS Type is Custom), Path: jagboot.rom, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the PDP11 emulator to libretro. This core emulates the Soviet Electronica BK computers series, including the BK-0010, BK-0010.01 and BK-0011(M), as well as the Terak 8510/a, which is a 1976 American PDP-11/03 platform that the Electronica BK series were designed after. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A significantly modified fork of Mednafen's Playstation emulator, this core differs from the -HW version by focusing on software rendering (i.e., instead of hardware-accelerated rendering). The software renderer is more accurate than the OpenGL and Vulkan renderers used in the -HW core, but it lacks some of the cosmetic options and performs any internal resolution increases on the CPU instead of the GPU, which is very demanding (devices with fast CPUs may reach 2x scale but nothing can maintain full speed at 4x at the time of this writing). Both varieties of Beetle-PSX are more accurate than PCSX-ReARMed but also significantly slower, so they are generally a better choice for higher-specced devices that can benefit from the additional features and accuracy while maintaining full speed.
