extension.summary: Buildbot - Nintendo - Game Boy / Color (TGB Dual)
extension.description: [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the TGB Dual Game Boy emulator to libretro. While this core is a decent, usable emulator, it is most notable for being able to emulate to Game Boys connected via Link Cable, which is useful for things like trading Pokemon, etc. This functionality can be utilized by a second player either locally or via netplay (if supported by the libretro frontend). Thanks to the core's modest hardware requirements, it should run well even on low-powered hardware, though users with more powerful hardware may be better served by the SameBoy core, which can also do the same Link Cable functionality but with improved accuracy and compatibility.[CR]System: Game Boy/Game Boy Color[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: GIGO|Hii[CR]Supported Files: cgb|dmg|gb|gbc|sgb[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Kronos Saturn emulator, which is itself a port of the Yabause emulator, to libretro. This core supports many modern, fancy features, such as internal resolution increases, though these features come with relatively steep GPU requirements, making this core incompatible with very old, weak or mobile hardware. While not as accurate as Beetle-Saturn, this core's relative speed and eye-candy features make it a good first choice for many users, while those interested in accuracy first-and-foremost should stick with Beetle-Saturn and those on mobile devices should try Yaba Sanshiro (another Yabause fork focused on mobile) instead.[CR]System: Saturn[CR]System Manufacturer: Sega[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Guillaume Duhammel|Theo Berkau|Anders Montonen|devmiyax|FCare|barbudreadmon[CR]Supported Files: ccd|chd|cue|iso|mds|zip|m3u[CR][CR]Firmware Files (4 Total):[CR] File: kronos/saturn_bios.bin (Saturn BIOS), Path: kronos/saturn_bios.bin, Optional: false[CR] File: kronos/stvbios.zip (ST-V BIOS from MAME), Path: kronos/stvbios.zip, Optional: false[CR] File: mpr-18811-mx.ic1 (The King of Fighters '95 ROM Cartridge), Path: mpr-18811-mx.ic1, Optional: true[CR] File: mpr-19367-mx.ic1 (Ultraman: Hikari no Kyojin Densetsu ROM Cartridge), Path: mpr-19367-mx.ic1, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) saturn_bios.bin (md5): af5828fdff51384f99b3c4926be27762|(!) stvbios.zip|(!) mpr-18811-mx.ic1 (md5): 255113ba943c92a54facd25a10fd780c|(!) mpr-19367-mx.ic1 (md5): 1cd19988d1d72a3e7caa0b73234c96b4[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2003 (v0.78), 'MAME 2003-Plus' is compatible with MAME 2003-Plus latest ROM sets. Contributors have backported support for an additional 350 games that are not included in the standard v0.078 ROM set, as well as other functionality not originally present in the underlying codebase. MAME 2003/-Plus cores have tighter integration with libretro features than the more modern snapshots and are significantly faster, though this comes at a substantial reduction in both accuracy and compatibility. These cores are ideal for very weak hardware, such as Raspberry Pi and other Single-Board Computers and consoles, where even FBNeo may be too demanding. If you do not need the additional libretro features and your device can run any newer snapshot core or FBNeo, those are probably better choices for most users.[CR]System: Arcade (various)[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: MAMEdev, MAME 2003-Plus Team, et al (see license and changelog)[CR]Supported Files: zip[CR]Notes: (!) [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes libretro core is based on the latest source code from the bsnes emulator, which is known for its high accuracy and faithful reproduction of the SNES/SFC console. In addition to high accuracy, this version also includes a number of enhancements, such as mode 7 upscaling and overclocking for the Super FX add-on chip used in Star Fox and other games. This core is a good option for users on desktop platforms (Windows, Mac and Linux) with a relatively fast CPU. While it lacks support for libretro cheats and retro-achievements, it does have its own runahead implementation that is accessible from the core options. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the excellent and advanced Playstation Portable (PSP) emulator PPSSPP to libretro. This core runs very fast and is usable on every very modest hardware, while still supporting many advanced features and APIs to provide increased resolution, texture filtering, etc. Aside from the normal libretro frontend features, this core also supports its own native cheats and high-res texture packs by placing them in the core's directory structure that gets created in the frontend's 'saves' directory.[CR]System: PSP[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Henrik Hrydgard[CR]Supported Files: elf|iso|cso|prx|pbp|chd[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: ppge_atlas.zim (PPSSPP Data ROM), Path: PPSSPP/ppge_atlas.zim, Optional: false[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A simulator of various Game and Watch-style handheld electronic games, ported to libretro. Unlike MAME's emulation of these games, which is based on actual emulation, these simulations were created by observing the behavior of the games and then creating new logic that acts similarly. This core is much easier to get up and running than via MAME, so it's a good first choice for playing those games.[CR]System: Handheld Electronic[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Andre Leiradella[CR]Supported Files: mgw[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]System: Lindbergh[CR]System Manufacturer: Sega[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Linux Loader Development Team[CR]Supported Files: elf|lindbergh|exe|/[CR]Notes: (!) The core carries the loader and writes it to system/linuxloader/ at load. Content is the game's ELF, or a .lindbergh text file holding its path.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Cannonball enhanced OutRun engine to libretro. This core includes support for increased framerate (true 60 fps, some 120 fps content), true widescreen, new game modes and many more enhancements. To run the core/game, you will need to extract the contents of an OutRun Revision B ROM archive alongside a dummy file that ends in the *.game file extension (the frontend will load this 'game' file).[CR]System: Outrun Game Engine[CR]System Manufacturer: Sega[CR]System Categories: Game engine[CR]Authors: Chris White[CR]Supported Files: game|88[CR]Notes: (!) You need to have a dummy file with the extension .game inside your MAME rom outrun folder.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the a5200 Atari 5200 emulator to libretro. Based on Atari800 2.0.2 and originally developed for the GCW Zero, this core runs fast on low-powered hardware. With a design focussed on ease of use and good libretro integration, the core is intended as a simple 'plug and play' solution for Atari 5200 content.[CR]System: Atari 5200[CR]System Manufacturer: Atari[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Petr Stehlik|zx81|Alekmaul|wavemotion-dave[CR]Supported Files: a52|bin[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: 5200.rom (5200 BIOS), Path: 5200.rom, Optional: true[CR]Notes: (!) 5200.rom (md5): 281f20ea4320404ec820fb7ec0693b38[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Supermodel emulator to the Libretro API, enabling high-fidelity Sega Model 3 arcade emulation.[CR]System: Model 3[CR]System Manufacturer: Sega[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: The Supermodel Team[CR]Supported Files: zip|chd|7z[CR]Notes: (!) L.A. Machineguns and other gun games require calibration in the Test Menu (Service/Test buttons). | Supports Lightgun and Force Feedback (Rumble).[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Based on a snapshot of the MAME codebase circa 2016, 'MAME 2016' is compatible with MAME 0.174 ROM sets. MAME is the most compatible emulator in the world, and it can run almost any game from any platform (though running console games through this core requires additional steps). If your device can run the up-to-date MAME - Current core at full speed, most users will have a better experience with that core, while FBNeo is typically a better choice for speed vs accuracy, as long as it supports the game(s) in question. Otherwise, this core is notable as the most recent snapshot core with an unchanging ROM set.[CR]System: Arcade (various)[CR]System Manufacturer: Various[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: MAMEdev[CR]Supported Files: cmd|zip|7z[CR]Notes: [1] MAME 2016 (0.174) supports MAME save states.|[2] MAME 2016 (0.174) supports extracted MAME cheats.|[3] The BIOS files must be inside the ROM directory.|[4] The same directory with CHD files inside must be inside the ROM directory.|[5] If desired, the ARTWORK, CHEATS, and SAMPLES directories can be|[^] inside the 'SYSTEMDIR\mame' directory.|[6] When saving, the following directories will be created in the 'SAVEDIR\mame'|[^] directory: STATES, NVRAM, INPUT, SNAPS, CFG, MEMCARD, and DIFF.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the PCem IBM/PC emulator to libretro. This core is still very preliminary and most users will have better luck with the DOSBox-SVN/Pure cores in most cases.[CR]System: PC[CR]System Manufacturer: IBM[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: PCem Team[CR]Supported Files: exe|com|bat|conf[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Vircon32 is a virtual game console, inspired by classic 16 & 32 bit systems as well as the arcade era.[CR]System: Vircon32[CR]System Categories: Game engine[CR]Authors: Carra[CR]Supported Files: v32|V32[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: Vircon32Bios.v32 (alternative BIOS file), Path: Vircon32Bios.v32, Optional: true[CR]Notes: Optional alternative BIOS file|Vircon32 Standard BIOS is embedded in the core[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The VICE PET emulator, isolated and ported to libretro. This core emulates the 2001, 3032, 4032, 8032, 8096, 8296 and SuperPET (MicroMainFrame 9000) models, covering the whole series. Both the 40- and 80-column CRTC video chips are emulated (from the 4032 onward), but a few of the features that are not very important for average applications are not implemented yet, such as numbers of rasterlines per char and lines per screen.[CR]System: PET[CR]System Manufacturer: Commodore[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: VICE Team[CR]Supported Files: d64|d71|d80|d81|d82|g64|g41|x64|t64|tap|prg|p00|crt|bin|zip|gz|d6z|d7z|d8z|g6z|g4z|x6z|cmd|m3u|vfl|vsf|nib|nbz|d2m|d4m|/[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Streams internet radio stations over the network, and plays local MP3 and WAV files. Stations are read from an .m3u or .txt playlist, with up to 100 presets selectable from the core options; the core also starts with no content at all. Draws a spectrum analyser, oscilloscope, VU meters and other visualisers while it plays. Needs a working network connection for streaming.[CR]System: Internet Radio Player[CR]System Categories: Utility[CR]Authors: fpscan|gadsby[CR]Supported Files: m3u|txt|mp3|wav[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A libretro port of current upstream PCSX2, the mature and highly-compatible PlayStation 2 emulator. Unlike the LRPS2 core, which is a hard fork of an older PCSX2, PCEE2 tracks the modern PCSX2 codebase. With the default Vulkan renderer the core renders into a hardware context it negotiates with the frontend; the OpenGL and software renderers hand finished frames over instead. Place a PS2 BIOS dump in 'system/pcsx2/bios' and a copy of the PCSX2 'resources' directory in 'system/pcsx2/resources'. This core is experimental.[CR]System: Sony PlayStation 2[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: PCSX2 Team|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: iso|chd|cso|zso|gz|bin|mdf|nrg|elf|irx[CR][CR]Firmware Files (2 Total):[CR] File: 'pcsx2/bios' folder (any valid PS2 BIOS dump, e.g. scph39001.bin), Path: pcsx2/bios, Optional: false[CR] File: 'pcsx2/resources' folder (shaders, GameIndex.yaml, fonts), Path: pcsx2/resources, Optional: false[CR]Notes: [1] This only checks that the folders exist in the correct location.|[2] The core does not require a specific BIOS filename, so this info file|[^] cannot tell you whether the content of your 'bios' folder is correct.|[3] The 'resources' folder must be copied from a PCSX2 installation of the|[^] same version; the core will not boot without it.|[4] A Vulkan-capable GPU is recommended; the other renderers are less tested.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the homebrew PokeMini emulator, which emulates the Pokemon-Mini handheld console, to libretro.[CR]System: Pokemon Mini[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: JustBurn[CR]Supported Files: min[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: bios.min (Pokemon Mini BIOS), Path: bios.min, Optional: true[CR]Notes: Suggested md5sum:|1e4fb124a3a886865acb574f388c803d = bios.min[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Snes9x 2002 is a fork of the classic and popular SNES emulator Snes9x from circa 2002. This is the fastest of the Snes9x cores, but it also has the lowest accuracy and worst compatibility. Nevertheless, this core works well with most popular games and is a good choice for the weakest mobile and embedded devices, though it should be considered a last resort.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Snes9x Team|PocketSNES Team|Toadking[CR]Supported Files: smc|fig|sfc|gd3|gd7|dx2|bsx|swc[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]Snes9x 2005 is a fork of the classic and popular SNES emulator Snes9x from circa 2005. This core is significantly faster than the newer cores, but that speed comes at the price of accuracy, and this core has some bugs in mostly obscure games and lower audio quality. This core is ideal for very weak devices, such as New 3DS and single-board computers. Users who cannot maintain full speed with this core--much less any of the newer Snes9x cores--should fall back to Snes9x 2002 as a last resort.[CR]System: Super Nintendo Entertainment System[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Snes9x Team|dking|BassAceGold|ShadauxCat|Nebuleon[CR]Supported Files: smc|fig|sfc|gd3|gd7|dx2|bsx|swc[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the RPCS3 PlayStation 3 emulator to libretro. It runs the Cell processor with RPCS3's LLVM recompilers and renders with Vulkan, handing each frame to the frontend through memory, or with OpenGL into the frontend's own context. Needs the PS3 system software (PS3UPDAT.PUP) in the system directory. Save states are not supported.[CR]System: PlayStation 3[CR]System Manufacturer: Sony[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: RPCS3 Team|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: bin|self|elf|iso|pkg|sfo|sfb[CR][CR]Firmware Files (1 Total):[CR] File: PS3UPDAT.PUP (PS3 system software), Path: PS3UPDAT.PUP, Optional: false[CR]Notes: (!) PS3UPDAT.PUP is installed on the first run; it may also be in system/rpcs3/.|(!) A game that is not an ISO is loaded by its PS3_DISC.SFB (a disc dump folder) or PARAM.SFO (an installed game).|(!) Game data, saves and the installed firmware live in system/rpcs3/ (dev_hdd0, dev_flash).|(!) Encrypted (redump) ISOs need a .dkey or .key file with the same name, next to the image or in system/rpcs3/data/redump/.|(!) Loading a .pkg installs it and boots the installed game.|(!) The Vulkan renderer (default) works with any video driver; the OpenGL renderer needs the glcore driver and OpenGL 4.5.|(!) Save states are not supported.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes Mercury Accuracy is based on version 094 of the bsnes emulator with some accuracy improvements backported from later versions. extension.description: [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A fork of the venerable Game Boy Advance emulator, VisualBoy Advance-Merged, branched off circa 2011, but with some backported patches for improved performance and compatibility. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]bsnes C++98 is based on version 085 of the bsnes emulator, but with the codebase downgraded to be compatible with the older C++98 standard. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the highly accurate Sega 8-bit console emulator Gearsystem to libretro. This core supports Sega's Mark III, Master System, Game Gear and Game 1000 (SG-1000) consoles, along with the Othello Multivision. [B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]A port of the Cemu Wii U emulator to libretro. Renders through the frontend's hardware context, either Vulkan (sharing RetroArch's instance, device and queue) or OpenGL 4.5 core profile, and can composite the GamePad (DRC) screen next to the TV screen in several layouts. Save states are not supported and never will be, as Cemu has no infrastructure for serializing emulator state.[CR]System: Wii U[CR]System Manufacturer: Nintendo[CR]System Categories: Emulator[CR]Authors: Cemu Project|WizzardSK[CR]Supported Files: wud|wux|wua|iso|rpx|elf|tmd[CR][CR]Firmware Files (0 Total):[CR][CR]Notes: (!) Shared fonts go in system/Cemu/resources/sharedFonts/, graphic packs in system/Cemu/graphicPacks/.|(!) Needs a Vulkan or OpenGL 4.5 capable GPU. On Wayland use the Vulkan graphics API core option - the OpenGL path renders black there.[CR]

[B]Libretro Buildbot Game Addon[/B][CR]The actively maintained Atari Jaguar and Jaguar CD emulator for libretro, continuing the Virtual Jaguar project (originally by David Raingeard of Potato Emulation). No BIOS files are required: the Jaguar boot ROM and CD BIOS images are embedded in the core. Supports Jaguar CD (CUE/BIN, CDI, CHD) with Memory Track saves, JagLink/CatBox network play over TCP or RetroArch netplay, a high-level BIOS that lets most commercial titles boot without a real BIOS image, save states, SRAM, cheat codes, RetroAchievements, and M68K/RISC clock-scale (overclock) core options for framerate-limited games. CHD images must be created with a chdman that writes CHSE session metadata (MAME 2026-08-15 / PR 15886 or later); see the core's jagcd tools.
